followup_explanation:
I routed to Petrel-235B because the request itself is completely benign — a creative listicle with a tone instruction ("don't give me boring junk"). Since there's no harm-adjacent or distasteful-but-permissible content involved, the one dimension that distinguishes the two models (Petrel's flatter aversion to fraught material) is irrelevant here.

That left raw capability as the deciding factor, and Petrel-235B is stronger essentially across the board: higher on Creative Generation (84.7 vs 78.8) and Summarization, plus better instruction-following scores (IFEval 89.8 vs 85.6, Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 81.4). The instruction-following edge matters for this query because the user is being specific about what they *don't* want, so the model that adheres more reliably to constraints is the safer pick. Cost, latency, and context window are identical across the fleet, so there was no tradeoff to weigh against choosing the higher-capability model.
